mechanism: Chlorthalidone-induced hypokalemia and hyperuricemia may complicate mycophenolate therapy; mycophenolate undergoes enterohepatic recirculation which may be affected by diuretic-induced fluid/electrolyte changes.
action: Monitor serum potassium, uric acid, and mycophenolate efficacy; consider potassium supplementation or alternative antihypertensive if significant electrolyte derangements occur.
